<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD is a standard Arch Linux package definition for an Electron/Node.js application. It declares a single source entry pointing to the project's own GitHub release tarball with a pinned sha256 checksum. No `pkgver()` function exists, and there are no top-level command substitutions, `eval`, `curl`, `wget`, or other constructs that would execute code when the PKGBUILD is sourced. The `build()` and `package()` functions contain the actual build/install logic, but they are not executed under `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` or `makepkg --printsrcinfo`. Fetching and verifying the upstream tarball is exactly what these commands are designed to do and poses no risk.
</details>

Standard PKGBUILD; no code executes during source fetch/parse.

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD for frank-go follows standard practices for packaging an Electron application. It downloads the source tarball from the project's official GitHub release, verifies it with a provided SHA256 checksum, and builds the application using npm commands (ci, bundle, prune). The package() function installs the built application files, creates a launcher script for system electron, and installs a desktop file and icon. There is no evidence of malicious behavior such as unauthorized network requests, obfuscated code, or unexpected system modifications. The application's runtime behavior of downloading the KataGo engine is documented as part of its upstream functionality and is not performed during the build process.
</details>
